title_ja: 損害保険ジャパン及びＳＯＭＰＯホールディングスに対する行政処分
title_en: Administrative action against Sompo Japan and Sompo Holdings
summary_en: On 25 January 2024, Japan's Financial Services Agency issued business improvement orders to Sompo Japan and Sompo Holdings over the insurer's handling of the Bigmotor fraudulent-claims scandal. It cited governance and internal-control failures, including resuming referrals of damaged vehicles to Bigmotor and not reporting key facts to the regulator. Both firms must submit improvement plans by 15 March 2024 and report progress quarterly, with the first reporting reference date at end of May 2024.

summary_en: On 28 June 2024, Japan's Financial Services Agency published the results of an additional investigation into premium-adjustment conduct by four major non-life insurers (Aioi Nissay Dowa, Sompo Japan, Tokio Marine & Nichido, Mitsui Sumitomo), following its 26 December 2023 business improvement orders. As of 14 June 2024, 600 policyholders were reported as involved in conduct likely violating or inconsistent with the Antimonopoly Act, up from 576. The FSA will keep requiring the insurers to implement their improvement plans.
